title: Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone Announce the Launch of Two Investment Solutions, Simplifying Access to Public and Private Markets
summary: Press releases, portfolio company news, and timely updates on our business.
body_text: Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone Announce the Launch of Two Investment Solutions, Simplifying Access to Public and Private Markets July 22, 2026 Funds available at launch through Bank of America wealth management platforms BOSTON, VALLEY FORGE, AND NEW YORK, July 22, 2026 – Wellington Management (“Wellington”), Vanguard, and Blackstone (NYSE: BX) today announced the launch of two new investment solutions created as part of their recently formed strategic alliance and designed to give eligible investors simplified access to professionally managed portfolios that combine public and private markets. WVB All Markets Fund, a multi-asset solution for investors who want to simplify the integration of public and private markets. The fund will integrate Wellington’s expertise in active public equities, Vanguard’s strengths in active fixed income and index strategies, with exposure to Blackstone’s leading perpetual private markets platform. The fund will trade under the tickers WVBIX, WVBAX, and WVBMX. WVB Blackstone All Privates Fund, a professionally managed solution providing a simple access point to Blackstone’s leading perpetual private markets platform, including private equity, private infrastructure, private real estate, and private credit in a single allocation. The new closed-end funds will be available at launch to Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank clients, providing advisors on one of the industry’s leading wealth management platforms with access to the first solutions from the strategic alliance. The alliance also anticipates broad participation and adoption from the RIA community, and will explore additional distribution opportunities across the wealth ecosystem over time. The solutions aim to help advisors build more diversified portfolios for high-net-worth and mass-affluent clients in a simplified investment framework. The funds are intended to help advisors construct long-term portfolios that seek strong performance, long-term growth, and broad portfolio diversification. A Powerful Alliance of Investment Leaders The WVB All Markets Fund and WVB Blackstone All Privates Fund bring together: Wellington’s nearly 100-year heritage of active management, fundamental research, and multi-asset allocation expertise; Vanguard’s 50-year legacy of delivering high-performing active strategies and index funds[ 1 ] with a relentless focus on cost efficiency and investor outcomes; and Blackstone’s 40-year track record of cycle-tested performance and leadership position as the world’s largest alternative asset manager and number one provider of private markets solutions for individuals. Together, the firms are uniquely positioned to deliver integrated investment solutions that were historically available primarily to large institutions. To expand access to their collective strengths, Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone are actively exploring additional product structures to support retirement savers, financial advisors, and individual investors. Mark Sutterlin, Head of Alternative Investments, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank, said: “Our clients are increasingly seeking broader access to private markets and for thoughtful ways to implement these strategies over time. Our scale and integrated platforms are expanding access to differentiated investment opportunities that can support more resilient long-term portfolios.” Jean M. Hynes, CEO and Managing Partner, Wellington Management, said: “The launch of the WVB All Markets and WVB Blackstone All Privates Funds reflects the strength of our strategic alliance with Vanguard and Blackstone. By combining our deep active management and asset allocation capabilities with Vanguard’s scale and expertise in fixed income and indexing and Blackstone’s leadership in private markets, we are delivering thoughtfully constructed solutions designed to meet investors’ evolving needs. We are particularly pleased to introduce these funds initially through the powerful Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank platforms.” Greg Davis, President and CIO of Vanguard, said: “For five decades, Vanguard has worked to improve investor outcomes through disciplined active management, low-cost index strategies, and a client-focused approach. Through this collaboration with Wellington and Blackstone, we are extending that mission into integrated public and private market solutions. Launching these funds with Bank of America Private Bank and Merrill is an important first step in expanding access to those solutions.” Jon Gray, President and COO of Blackstone, said: “Blackstone has delivered performance in private markets for individuals for more than two decades, helping them access the premium returns, lower volatility, and diversification that private markets can provide. These new solutions bring together the performance and scale of Blackstone’s private markets platform with the exceptional strengths of Wellington and Vanguard, creating simple and comprehensive access for advisors and their clients to help build long-term wealth.” [ 1 ] For the 10-year period ending June 30, 2026, 77% of Vanguard funds outperformed the average return of their peer group, or 260 of 336 Vanguard funds. Results will vary for other time periods. Only funds with a minimum ten-year history were included in the comparison. Source: LSEG Lipper. Note that the competitive performance data shown represent past performance, which is not a guarantee of future results, and that all investments are subject to risks. For the most recent performance, visit our website at www.vanguard.com/performance . Wellington is the investment manager of the funds. Blackstone and Vanguard are not sponsors, promoters, investment advisers, sub-advisers, underwriters, or affiliates of the funds. About Wellington Management Wellington Management is one of the world’s largest independent investment management firms, serving as a trusted adviser to over 2,500 clients in more than 60 countries. The firm manages more than US$1.35 trillion, as of April 30, 2026, for pensions, endowments and foundations, insurers, family offices, fund sponsors, global wealth managers, and other clients. Wellington aspires to provide excellent service to clients through a unique combination of independence enabled by its distinctive private partnership model, diverse perspectives through its unified, multi-asset investment platform, and relentless curiosity and intellectual rigor fostered by its enduring collaborative culture. For more information, visit wellington.com . About Vanguard Founded in 1975, Vanguard is one of the world's leading investment management companies. The firm offers investments, advice, and retirement services to tens of millions of individual investors around the globe—directly, through workplace plans, and through financial intermediaries. Vanguard operates under a unique, investor-owned structure and adheres to a simple purpose: to give investors the best chance for investment success. For more information, visit vanguard.com . About Blackstone Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com . Important disclosures Wellington Management, Vanguard and Blackstone are not affiliated. (together with its affiliates, “Blackstone”) or by The Vanguard Group, Inc. or its affiliates (together with its affiliates, “Vanguard”), as applicable. Interests in certain Underlying Funds are illiquid and may only be redeemed during periodic repurchase offers pursuant to which such Underlying Funds repurchase limited amounts of their outstanding shares at the Underlying Fund’s discretion. An Underlying Fund may accept less than the amount of Underlying Fund shares that the Fund tenders in a repurchase offer. There is no regular market for interests in such Underlying Funds, which typically must be sold in privately negotiated transactions. Any such sales would likely require the consent of the Underlying Fund’s manager and could occur at a discount to the stated NAV. If the Advisor determines to cause the Fund to sell its interest in an Underlying Fund, the Fund may be unable to sell such interest quickly, if at all, and could therefore be obligated to continue to hold such interest for an extended period of time, or to accept a lower price for a more expeditious sale. title: Age-appropriate chores for kids: a chore chart that builds executive function skills
summary: Age-appropriate chores for kids, by age, plus how to run a chore chart that builds executive function skills like planning, working memory, and follow-through.
body_text: The chore chart by age Match the job to where your child's executive function actually is, not where you wish it were. A two-year-old can't plan a sequence yet; a ten-year-old is bored by a job with no ownership in it. Use these as a starting menu, then let your child help choose. Ages 2 to 3: one-step jobs, side by side Put toys in a bin Drop dirty clothes in the hamper Hand you groceries to put away Wipe a spill with a cloth At this age the win is simply following a single instruction to completion, alongside you. You're planting the idea that they're a contributor. Ages 4 to 5: two-step jobs, with a picture chart Set the table (napkins, then forks) Feed a pet with a measured scoop Make the bed, roughly Water plants This is where a picture chart earns its keep. Two steps in the right order is real planning for a preschooler. Ages 6 to 7: multi-step jobs they can start solo Pack their own snack and water bottle Sort laundry into lights and darks Clear and wipe the table after dinner Get the backpack ready the night before Task initiation is the focus now. The goal is starting on one cue instead of five reminders. Ages 8 to 9: jobs with a quality bar Load or unload the dishwasher Take out trash and recycling on the right day Vacuum a room Help make a simple meal from a recipe card Add a self-check step. "Recycling on the right day" quietly builds the calendar-awareness that homework planners will later demand. Ages 10 to 11: jobs they manage over time Do their own laundry start to finish Plan and prep one family meal a week Care for a pet's full routine Manage a weekly tidy of their room without prompting These stretch across days, so kids practice holding a goal in mind and monitoring their own progress, the core of long-project stamina. Ages 12 and up: jobs that mirror adult systems Run a grocery sub-list on a budget Manage their own schedule of jobs across the week Do yard work or deeper cleaning tasks Track and complete a recurring responsibility without a chart at all By now the chart itself should be fading. A teen who can run their responsibilities without an external tracker has internalized the executive-function skills you spent a decade building. Four mistakes that turn a chore chart into a battle Doing the planning for them. If you sequence every step, you're exercising your executive function, not theirs. Hand back the thinking. Too many jobs at once. Three consistent jobs beat ten sporadic ones. Overloading the chart guarantees it gets abandoned. Redoing their work in front of them. A wobbly bed made by a five-year-old is a win. Silently remaking it teaches them their effort doesn't count. Never fading the reminders. If you're still cueing every step months in, the chart has become your job. Shrink the prompt on purpose. Frequently asked questions Should chores be tied to allowance? Many families separate the two: some jobs are simply part of belonging to the household, while a few extra paid jobs can teach money skills. If you want to build financial habits alongside responsibility, see our guide to life skills to teach kids at home . What if my child has ADHD or struggles with getting started? Lean harder on the visual chart, shorten the jobs, and make the first cue playful rather than nagging. Our roundup of executive function activities for kids has more that pairs well with a chore routine. My kid just refuses. Now what? Drop the count to one job, do it together for a week, and give them a real choice in which job it is. Ownership beats enforcement almost every time. Where classes fit in Chores build the executive-function foundation. Structured classes give kids another place to practice the same planning-and-follow-through muscles with a teacher who's watching for them. If you want to understand the skill you're building before you build it, start with what executive function is and why it matters , and see how play-based learning builds life skills from a different angle. When you're ready, a live small-group class on Outschool can give your child a low-stakes place to practice organization and independence outside the home. Sources [1] Diamond, A. (2013). Executive Functions. Annual Review of Psychology. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4084861/ [2] American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org. Chores and Responsibility. https://www.healthychildren.org/English/family-life/family-dynamics/communication-discipline/Pages/Chores-and-Children.aspx

title: Cloaked vs. Optery (2026 Comparison): Which Data Removal Service is Best?
summary: If your top priority is removing your personal information from data brokers, Optery remains the clear leader, offering a deeper, more transparent, and more comprehensive service than Cloaked. If, however, you're looking for an all-in-one privacy toolkit in a single subscription, Cloaked delivers a broader set of capabilities. For consumers who want the strongest data broker removal available without giving up those additional privacy tools, using Optery alongside Cloaked can provide the best of both worlds.
body_text: Who Is Cloaked? Cloaked is a multi-feature privacy app. It bundles email/phone aliases, spam-call blocking, a password manager, VPN, $1M identity theft insurance, dark web monitoring, and a basic personal data removal service all in one subscription. This bundle is genuinely appealing. Who Is Optery? Optery is #1 most effective and award winning personal data removal service . Optery’s sole focus is personal data removal from data brokers, and it performs this function better than any other company in the industry, including Cloaked. This is why CNET named Optery “Editors’ Choice” and the #1 best overall personal data removal service of 2026 , why Optery was the #1 most effective personal data removal service tested in a Consumer Reports benchmark study , and why Optery is the only personal data removal service to have won the PCMag “Editors’ Choice” award for personal data removal every year from 2022 – 2026. Which Should You Choose? If you’re interested in a well-rounded privacy bundle, encompassing email/phone aliases, spam-call blocking, a password manager, VPN, $1M identity theft insurance, dark web monitoring, and a basic personal data removal service all in one, then Cloaked is the better choice. However, if your main concern is personal data removal from data brokers, Optery is by the better choice. Cloaked does have a personal data removal service capability, but it is not as comprehensive or robust as Optery in this area. As one Redditor said “Although they (Cloaked) also include data removal, I found it to be far less intuitive and the communication (as far as what exactly the status was for removals) compared to Optery, who’s sole focus is to search for and remove your data from brokers.” Another option to consider is to use both services simultaneously, supplementing Cloaked’s well-rounded bundle with Optery’s industry-leading personal data removal service. Cloaked vs. Optery according to a Redditor Read on for a more detail comparison of Cloaked vs Optery. “Optery is our pick for best overall data removal service because it’s easy to use and it’s better than any other service at showing you the work it does to remove your data. It also had the highest removal success rate according to Consumer Reports’ testing.” Zachary McAuliffe Senior Writer, CNET 💡 Important Note to Current Customers of Cloaked: Existing Cloaked customers can create a free Optery account and review the results of the free Optery Exposure Report scan to test Cloaked’s performance and double-check Cloaked’s work. Based on our research and testing, Optery finds ~50 exposed profiles for customers of other personal data removal services on average. Executive Summary Best fit for Cloaked: People who want one subscription that bundles email and phone aliases, a password manager, spam call blocking, VPN, identity theft insurance, and a basic personal data removal service all in one subscription. Best fit for Optery: People who want the #1 most effective personal data removal service on the market, or who want to take a “best of breed” approach, selecting the best product on the market for each functional area, e.g. the best VPN, Password Manager, Identity Theft Insurance, Personal Data Removal, etc – all from different “best of breed” vendors. Cloaked Strengths: Broad feature bundle beyond data removal (aliases, Call Guard, dark web and SSN monitoring, $1M identity theft insurance), a straightforward flat-rate family plan, and independently verified security certifications (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, PCI DSS v4.0.1). Cloaked Limitations: No ongoing free tier (only a lead-generation “free scan”), no public before-and-after screenshot verification of data broker removals, more limited data broker removal coverage than Optery. Optery Strengths: A genuinely free Free Basic account with screenshots, clearly published plan-by-plan broker counts, most comprehensive and effective data broker removal coverage in the industry, unlimited Custom Removals Requests, Blur Your Home on Google Maps and Apple Maps, and screenshot-based removal verification on paid plans. Flexible billing options: Monthly, Yearly, and the ability to Pause / Resume / Upgrade / Downgrade subscriptions at any time. Also offers a straight-forward family plan, and industry leading security certification (SOC 2 Type 2). Optery Limitations: Does not offer privacy bundle features beyond personal data removal at this time. Who should choose which service: Cloaked can suit someone who wants one subscription for aliases and a light-weight personal data removal function together. Optery fits better for anyone who wants the most comprehensive, effective, and robust personal data removal, with verifiable proof of removal screenshots. Quick Verdict Category Cloaked Optery Free scan or free tier Free “Data Safety Scan” requires a phone number; no continuous free scan/removal account Free Basic account, no credit card required, with free quarterly Exposure Reports Screenshot verification Not Available Exposure and Removals Reports include screenshots on paid plans (Extended and Ultimate plan) Automated broker coverage 354 sites tagged “Data Broker” specifically on Cloaked’s own site directory, out of 1,000+ total sites listed. The rest of their list is tagged for “Other websites”, e.g. sites like The Cheesecake Factory (huh???) Optery offers completely transparent pricing and feature list on its Pricing page. Subscription plans start at $3.99 / month or $39 per year for 380+ data broker sites, all the way up to $24.99 per month or $249 per year for 950+ data broker sites (or 405 without enabling Expanded Reach ). Reporting cadence Continuous monitoring and Automated scans. Progress is tracked through In-App Dashboard Real Time Reporting viewable through In-App Dashboard with Quarterly Removal Reports (with Before and After Screenshots) for Extended and Ultimate Plans; Free Quarterly Exposure Reports for Free Tier 1. What Cloaked Does Well Cloaked deserves credit on several fronts, based on what its own site and independent coverage confirm. A genuinely bundled privacy suite. Cloaked pairs data broker removal with unlimited email and phone aliases, a password manager, spam call blocking, VPN, dark web and SSN monitoring, and $1 million in identity theft insurance, all in one subscription. For someone who wants a single app rather than several separate tools, that is a real convenience. Simple household pricing. Cloaked’s Family plan covers up to four people for $24.99 per month billed annually, with the full feature set included for everyone on the plan. For a household that wants aliases and light removal together, this is easy to understand. Verified security certifications. Cloaked’s trust page documents ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certification, a completed PCI DSS v4.0.1 audit, and SOC 2 Type 2 compliance. These are checkable credentials, not just marketing language. Included identity theft insurance. Cloaked’s homepage states coverage of up to $1 million in financial losses from identity theft and fraud, included standard rather than sold as an add-on. For users who place a premium on this kind of backstop, this is a real differentiator from removal-only competitors. A large total site directory. Cloaked’s own site-coverage page lists 1,000+ individual sites it monitors and works to remove data from, spanning both data brokers and other companies (retailers, employers, and similar organizations) that may hold a person’s contact information. For users who mainly want a bundled privacy app, aliases for everyday sign-ups, and basic broker cleanup as one part of a bigger toolkit, this may be enough. 2. In the Realm of Personal Data Removal Cloaked Falls Short If your interest is in personal data removal from data brokers, based on Cloaked’s website, several gaps are worth understanding before you subscribe. Coverage numbers vary, and coverage numbers are inflated with a puzzling set of sites. Cloaked’s site-coverage directory, when filtered to the “Data Broker” category specifically, lists 354 sites. The same directory’s total count, across data brokers and “other websites” (mainstream consumer/business sites), is 1,000+, including sites like The Cheesecake Factory and UCLA Health (?). Separately, Cloaked’s enterprise page states data is removed from “400+ data brokers”. Optery covers 950+ data brokers, and doesn’t inflate its list with sites like The Cheesecake Factory and UCLA Health. Cloaked Data Broker Coverage No visible screenshot-based removal verification. Before-and-after screenshots showing that a specific profile was found and later removed are not available. This may not matter to every user, but it is a notable limitation for anyone who wants independent, verifiable evidence instead of relying on a running counter. Optery provides before-and-after screenshot evidence, proving its work in its Removals Reports. The “free scan” is a lead-generation tool, not an ongoing free tier. Cloaked’s homepage free scan asks for a phone number and produces an exposure report, but it’s not a persistent free account with continued monitoring, comparable to a free tier you could use indefinitely without paying. If you want free, ongoing visibility into your exposure, this is a limitation. Optery offers a Free Basic account tier for free self-service removals tools and free ongoing Exposure Reports with screenshots. Regional coverage is limited. Cloaked’s own footer states the service is “currently available in the USA and Canada.” This may not matter for most US-based buyers, but it is worth knowing if you need coverage elsewhere. Optery is currently available in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa. 3. Data Broker Coverage Comparison Coverage question Cloaked Optery Public broker list available? Yes, a filterable directory exists, tagging each entry as “Data Broker” or “Other website” Yes, Optery publishes a named list of sites for each plan tier directly on its pricing page Data broker-specific count 354 (Individual, Couple, Family) 400+ (Enterprise) Optery offers a range of plans starting at $3.99 per month, or $39 per year to $24.99 per month, or $249 per year, covering 380+ data broker sites to 635+ data broker sites (or 405+ Sites without enabling Expanded Reach)and Unlimited Custom Removals (for a grand total of 950+ Sites covered) respectively Automated Data Broker Removals Count 354 (Individual, Couple, Family) 400+ (Enterprise) Automated removals are tier-specific (see above); Ultimate also allows unlimited Custom Removal Requests for 950+ Custom removals count or policy Not Available Ultimate plan: unlimited custom removal requests for sites outside the standard automated list, eligible after 30 days International or regional coverage US and Canada only United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa 4. Verification and Reporting for Personal Data Removal Verification is the difference between a service telling you it removed your data and showing you it did. Optery’s Exposure Reports show where a person’s profile appears at data broker and people-search sites, using what the company calls “patented view links” so users can see the profile without necessarily contacting the broker directly themselves. Optery adds Removals Reports approximately every 90 days that include before-and-after screenshots which is the only personal data removal service that provides detailed exposure and removal reports, complete with screenshots, to demonstrate the effectiveness of its services. Cloaked’s dashboard, per its help center, shows a running “Total records removed” count, “Days Protected,” and in-progress versus completed broker scans. This gives a user a sense of overall progress, but it is a different kind of evidence than a screenshot showing a specific profile disappearing from a specific site. Optery’s key advantage here is not just that it says removals happened, they also show where profiles were found and, later, screenshot evidence tied to the removal. That is a meaningfully more auditable model for a privacy professional who needs to document that a specific exposure was actually resolved, and it is also easier for an everyday consumer to understand at a glance. 5. Free Scan and Free Tier for Personal Data Removal What you get before paying Cloaked Optery Free scan available Yes, the homepage “Data Safety Scan” requires a phone number Yes, no credit card required to create a Free Basic account Persistent free account Free scan only. No standing account Yes, Free Basic is a standing account, not a one-time scan Actual exposed profiles shown The scan is described as producing a “personalized exposure report” showing where data is found Yes, Free Basic includes a Personalized Exposure Report with screenshots and view links to hundreds of sites Screenshots provided for free Not Available Yes, per Optery’s pricing page, Free Basic includes “Personalized Exposure Report with Screenshots” Self-service removal tools included free Cloaked routes users toward a paid subscription for removals after the Free Scan Yes, Free Basic includes self-service removal tools and shortcuts to broker opt-out pages Ongoing free monitoring Not Available Yes, free quarterly Exposure Reports continue for as long as the account remains active A free scan should help you make a decision, not just create anxiety. Cloaked’s free scan requires a phone number and produces an exposure report. Optery’s Free Basic account requires no credit card, includes a Personalized Exposure Report with screenshots, and continues with free quarterly reports for as long as the account stays active. 6. Pricing and Value Plan or tier Cloaked Optery Free option Free scan only (requires phone number) Free Basic account, no credit card required, ongoing Lowest paid plan Individual: $12.49/mo billed monthly, or $9.99/mo billed annually ($119.99/yr) Core: $3.99/mo billed monthly, or $3.25/mo billed annually ($39/yr) Mid-tier plan Couple: $19.99/mo billed monthly, or $14.99/mo billed annually ($174.99/yr), covers 2 people Extended: $14.99/mo billed monthly, or $12.42/mo billed annually ($149/yr), adds a human Privacy Agent and screenshot Removals Reports Highest consumer plan Family: $29.99/mo billed monthly, or $24.99/mo billed annually ($299.99/yr), covers up to 4 people Ultimate: $24.99/mo billed monthly, or $20.70/mo billed annually ($249/yr), for one person, with unlimited custom removals Family option Yes, Family plan bundles up to 4 people at one flat price, including full feature set (aliases, password manager, insurance, data removal) Yes, Optery for Family offers up to 30% off all plans. NO LIMIT to the number of people you can add. Business option Enterprise plan available; custom pricing via demo request; framed as an employee benefits bundle Optery for Business: Free PRO (free), Core PRO, Ultimate PRO, and a custom Enterprise tier (minimum 100 licenses) with SSO/SCIM/SAML included Money-back guarantee 30-day money-back guarantee 30-Day Money Back Guarantee for individual accounts (not available for business accounts) Optery also maintains a promo codes page for certain special circumstances and needs, offering a discount to groups such as military members and veterans, healthcare workers, teachers, seniors, students, and domestic violence or stalking victims, among others. 7. Consumer Reports and Independent Testing In August 2024, Consumer Reports evaluated the top people-search removal services, including Optery, DeleteMe, EasyOptOuts, IDX, Kanary, Confidently, and ReputationDefender. Cloaked was not part of this study, presumably because it did not have a strong offering in this category. Optery was the most effective service of all services tested at the end of the four-month blind study. While the Consumer Reports study was well-intentioned, it was poorly designed and had several problems, which Optery responded to in a public statement . 8. Awards for Personal Data Removal Optery’s awards and recognition is unparalleled in the personal data removal industry. A representative sample is listed below, with a fuller list on Optery’s Awards page here . CNET Editors’ Choice (2026) PCMag.com Editors’ Choice (2022 – 2026) Cybersecurity Excellence Award (2024 – 2026) SiliconANGLE TechForward Award for Digital Risk Protection (2025) Fortress Cybersecurity Award (2025 – 2026) Global InfoSec and Top InfoSec Innovator Awards by Cyber Defense Magazine (2024 – 2026) Fast Company “Next Big Things in Tech” for Security & Privacy (2023) Cloaked has also received recognitions: Fast Company’s 2024 World Changing Ideas Awards, Honorable Mention in the Small and Mighty category, recognizing Cloaked’s broader consumer privacy mission rather than a specific product or category ranking. Product Hunt, “Product of the Day”, awarded at Cloaked’s public launch out of beta in 2023. When a company is recognized across multiple, independently judged programs over several consecutive years by outlets that also cover competitors, that consistency adds useful context when evaluating vendor maturity. Optery stands on its own, with the most awards by far of any personal data removal service in the industry. 9. Best Fit: Who Should Choose Which for Personal Data Removal? title: CAE and Saab sign MoU to collaborate on comprehensive training and mission support solutions for the Gripen
summary: /CNW/ -- (NYSE: CAE) (TSX: CAE) CAE and Saab today announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on advanced training,...
body_text: MONTREAL , July 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- (NYSE: CAE) (TSX: CAE ) CAE and Saab today announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on advanced training, simulation, and mission support capabilities for the Gripen fighter aircraft in Canada should the Government of Canada choose to make the Gripen part of its future fighter capability. Under the proposed collaboration, CAE would play a key role in establishing and operating a Canadian-based training ecosystem for Gripen pilots and technicians, supporting advanced pilot training, simulator operations, technical training, and sustainment services. CAE and Saab would also explore opportunities to support mission systems development and sustainment in Canada, combining Saab's platform expertise with CAE's world-class training, simulation, and operational support solutions. "This agreement reflects a shared commitment to supporting Canada's long-term defence readiness, and we're proud to serve Canada's men and women in uniform through world-class training, simulation, and mission systems support," said Matthew Bromberg, CAE President and CEO. "Our collaboration with Saab can help strengthen Canada's future fighter capability while creating meaningful opportunities for Canadian engineers, technicians, and aviation professionals." "Saab's approach has always been to build real capability in the countries where we operate," said Micael Johansson, CEO of Saab. "Through this partnership with CAE, we would establish a world-class training and mission support capability in Canada, creating highly skilled jobs while ensuring critical knowledge, expertise, and operational data remain in Canadian hands." The agreement includes collaboration on research and development initiatives focused on next-generation capabilities, reinforcing a shared commitment to innovation, operational effectiveness, and long-term readiness. In addition to supporting potential future Gripen capabilities in Canada, the MoU opens opportunities for CAE and Saab to explore collaboration on Gripen-related training, mission support, and sustainment opportunities in international markets. About CAE At CAE , we exist to make the world safer. We deliver cutting-edge training, simulation, and critical operations solutions to prepare aviation professionals and defence forces for the moments that matter. Every day, we empower pilots, cabin crew, maintenance technicians, airlines, business aviation operators, and defence and security personnel to perform at their best and when the stakes are the highest. Around the globe, we're everywhere customers need us to be with sites and training locations in over 40 countries. For nearly 80 years, CAE has been at the forefront of innovation, consistently seeking to set the standard by delivering excellence in high-fidelity flight simulators and training solutions, while embedding sustainability at the heart of everything we do. By harnessing technology and enhancing human performance, we strive to be the trusted partner in advancing safety and mission readiness - today and tomorrow.
